# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

🌐 Web query:

`Python urllib.request.urlopen timeout default official documentation`

💡 Result:

According to the official Python documentation, the timeout parameter in urllib.request.urlopen specifies a timeout in seconds for blocking operations like the connection attempt [1][2][3]. If this parameter is not explicitly provided, the function uses the global default timeout setting [1][4][2]. This global default is determined by the socket module's default timeout [5][6]. By default, when the socket module is first imported, this value is set to None, which means that new socket objects have no timeout, effectively causing blocking operations to wait indefinitely [5][6]. You can check or modify this global default timeout using the following methods in the socket module: To get the current global default timeout: import socket print(socket.getdefaulttimeout) To set a global default timeout for all future socket objects: import socket socket.setdefaulttimeout(10.0) # Sets the global default to 10 seconds It is important to note that the timeout parameter in urllib.request.urlopen only applies to HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP connections [1][4][3].

Citations:

- 1: https://docs.python.org/3/library/urllib.request.html
- 2: https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/urllib.request.html
- 3: https://docs.python.org/3.10/library/urllib.request.html
- 4: https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/urllib.request.html
- 5: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/60440273/timeout-value-in-python-3-urlopen
- 6: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/29649173/what-is-the-global-default-timeout
